How to Import a Used Car from Germany to Nigeria

Importing a used car from Germany to Nigeria involves navigating import duties of 20-35% depending on engine size, clearing customs at Tin Can Island or Apapa Port in Lagos, and obtaining a Form M from an authorized dealer bank. The entire process takes 4-8 weeks from purchase to delivery at your local port.

Nigeria is the largest vehicle import market in West Africa, with over 400,000 used vehicles imported annually according to the Nigerian Customs Service (NCS). Germany ranks among the top 5 source countries for these imports, thanks to the quality of German-inspected vehicles and the availability of popular brands like Toyota, Mercedes-Benz, and Ford.

Nigeria Vehicle Import Duty Rates (2025)

The Nigerian Customs Service applies a tiered duty structure based on engine capacity and vehicle type. All rates are calculated on the CIF (Cost, Insurance, and Freight) value of the vehicle.

Vehicle TypeImport DutyVATSurchargeTotal Effective Rate
Cars (up to 1600cc)20%7.5%2%~35%
Cars (1600-2000cc)20%7.5%2%~35%
Cars (over 2000cc)20%7.5%5%~40%
SUVs and Trucks35%7.5%5%~55%
Commercial Vehicles10%7.5%2%~22%
Tractors5%7.5%0%~13%

These rates are based on the ECOWAS Common External Tariff (CET) and the Nigerian Finance Act. Rates may change with annual budget announcements, so always verify with the Nigeria Customs Service before finalizing your purchase.

Vehicle Age Restrictions

Nigeria does not impose a strict age limit on imported used vehicles, unlike Kenya (8-year limit) or Ghana (10-year limit). However, vehicles older than 15 years may face additional scrutiny during customs inspection and could attract higher insurance costs during shipping.

For the best import experience, RosM Autos recommends vehicles manufactured within the last 10 years. These tend to clear customs faster and retain higher resale value in the Nigerian market.

Required Documents for Vehicle Import to Nigeria

You need the following documents to clear a vehicle through Nigerian customs. Missing any of these will cause delays and potential storage fees at the port.

  1. Form M — Obtained through an authorized dealer bank in Nigeria. This is the import permit that must be opened before the vehicle ships.
  2. Bill of Lading — The shipping document issued by the carrier confirming your vehicle is on board.
  3. Commercial Invoice — Shows the purchase price, vehicle details, and seller information (provided by RosM Autos).
  4. Packing List — Details of the shipment contents if shipping by container.
  5. Insurance Certificate — Marine cargo insurance covering the transit.
  6. Pre-Arrival Assessment Report (PAAR) — Generated through the Nigeria Customs automated system after you submit your Form M and other documents.
  7. Vehicle Title / Export Certificate — German export documentation (Ausfuhrkennzeichen or Abmeldebescheinigung).
  8. SON Conformity Assessment Programme (SONCAP) Certificate — Required for new vehicles; used vehicles may need a Standards Organisation of Nigeria waiver.

Step-by-Step Import Process

Step 1: Choose Your Vehicle

Browse the RosM Autos inventory and select a quality-inspected vehicle. Every car in our catalog has passed a multi-point inspection covering engine, transmission, body, electronics, and interior condition. We provide detailed photos and a condition report before you commit.

Step 2: Open Form M with Your Bank

Visit an authorized dealer bank in Nigeria (Zenith Bank, GTBank, First Bank, or Access Bank are common choices) and open a Form M for vehicle importation. You will need the proforma invoice from RosM Autos, your passport, and your Tax Identification Number (TIN).

Step 3: Get Your All-In Quote

Contact RosM Autos with your destination port (Tin Can Island or Apapa, Lagos). We provide an all-inclusive quote covering the vehicle price, export documentation, marine insurance, and shipping costs. There are no hidden fees.

Step 4: Make Payment

Pay via bank transfer. RosM Autos confirms receipt and begins preparing the vehicle for export, including German deregistration and export plate processing.

Step 5: Shipping

We arrange RoRo (Roll-on/Roll-off) or container shipping from Bremerhaven or Hamburg port to Lagos. Transit time is typically 18-25 days depending on the shipping line and route. You receive a Bill of Lading and tracking information once the vehicle is loaded.

Step 6: Customs Clearance in Nigeria

Once the vessel arrives at Tin Can Island or Apapa Port, your customs broker processes the PAAR, pays duties through the Nigeria Customs automated payment system, and completes physical examination. This takes 5-14 business days depending on port congestion.

Step 7: Vehicle Registration

After clearing customs, register the vehicle with the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and obtain your Nigerian number plates through the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) verification process.

Shipping Costs: Germany to Lagos

Shipping costs vary by vehicle size, shipping method, and current freight rates. Here are typical ranges based on recent RosM Autos shipments:

RoRo is generally cheaper for single vehicles but offers less protection. Container shipping costs more but protects the vehicle from salt spray and allows you to ship spare parts or personal items alongside the car.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Not opening Form M before shipping — Without a valid Form M, your vehicle cannot clear customs. Always open this before the car leaves Germany.
  • Undervaluing the vehicle on the invoice — Nigerian Customs uses a benchmark pricing system. If your declared value is below their benchmark, they will reassess at a higher value and you may face penalties.
  • Choosing an inexperienced clearing agent — A good customs broker can save you days of delays and thousands in unnecessary fees. Ask for recommendations from other importers.
  • Ignoring demurrage fees — Containers at Tin Can Island incur storage fees after the free period (usually 7-14 days). Clear your vehicle promptly to avoid these charges.
  • Skipping marine insurance — RoRo shipments are exposed to the elements for 3+ weeks. Insurance typically costs 1.5-2% of the vehicle value and protects your entire investment.

  • Quality inspection — Every vehicle passes a multi-point condition check. Germany's TÜV inspection culture means cars are maintained to high standards throughout their life.
  • Complete documentation — We handle all German export paperwork including deregistration, export plates, and customs declarations.
  • Shipping coordination — Direct relationships with shipping lines at Bremerhaven and Hamburg mean competitive rates and reliable transit times.
  • Transparent pricing — All-inclusive quotes with no hidden fees. The price you see includes the vehicle, documentation, and shipping.
  • After-sale support — We provide tracking and assist with any questions during the customs clearance process.

faqItems.question: How much does it cost to import a used car to Nigeria from Germany?
faqItems.answer: The total cost depends on the vehicle price, shipping method, and engine size. For example, a 2018 Toyota Highlander priced at €12,500 would cost approximately €21,150 (₦33.8M) total including shipping, import duties (35% for SUVs), VAT (7.5%), surcharge, and clearing fees. Smaller vehicles with engines under 2000cc attract lower total duty rates of around 35%.

faqItems.question: What documents do I need to import a car to Nigeria?
faqItems.answer: You need: Form M (from your Nigerian bank), Bill of Lading, Commercial Invoice, Marine Insurance Certificate, Pre-Arrival Assessment Report (PAAR), the German export certificate, and optionally a SONCAP certificate. The Form M must be opened before the vehicle ships from Germany.

faqItems.question: Is there a vehicle age limit for imports to Nigeria?
faqItems.answer: Nigeria does not enforce a strict age limit on imported used vehicles, unlike Kenya (8 years) or Ghana (10 years). However, vehicles older than 15 years may face extra customs scrutiny and higher insurance costs. For the best experience, vehicles under 10 years old are recommended.

faqItems.question: How long does it take to ship a car from Germany to Nigeria?
faqItems.answer: Sea transit from Bremerhaven or Hamburg to Lagos (Tin Can Island or Apapa Port) takes 18-25 days by RoRo or container ship. Add 5-14 business days for customs clearance at the port, bringing the total delivery time to roughly 4-8 weeks from shipment.

faqItems.question: Should I use RoRo or container shipping to Nigeria?
faqItems.answer: RoRo (Roll-on/Roll-off) is cheaper, typically €800-€1,500 depending on vehicle size, but the car is exposed to elements during transit. Container shipping costs €1,500-€3,000 but offers full protection and lets you ship spare parts alongside the vehicle. For high-value vehicles, container shipping is recommended.

tldr: Importing a used car from Germany to Nigeria costs 35-55% in total duties on top of the vehicle and shipping price. You need a Form M from your bank before shipping, and the process takes 4-8 weeks total. RoRo shipping is cheaper but container offers better protection.
